The care crew and water breaks, minutes
It started on time, and the ramp lead led
Attending were Caleb Berg, Mateo Park, Maggie, the passenger coordinator, the cabin team, and the senior coordinator.

The team reviewed the travel steps for companion animals and kept the tone focused on calm, simple handoffs. The passenger coordinator noted that clear reminders at booking reduce stress for families and help the desk prepare carriers, documents, and feeding notes with care. <<FACT F097>> The group agreed that the main goal is to keep each traveler comfortable while also keeping records complete and easy to follow.

Discussion then moved to transfer support and the way staff should respond when plans change after acceptance. <<FACT F106>> The cabin team asked for tighter updates from the desk so that animal welfare checks and owner communication stay aligned during busy days. The senior coordinator added that handoffs work best when the notes are brief, accurate, and easy to read at a glance.

The final topic was check-in readiness, especially for travelers arriving with extra supplies or special instructions. <<FACT F092>> Staff agreed to keep the same friendly approach at the counter, offer steady reassurance, and flag any concerns early so they can be handled without delay. A short reminder list will be shared with the team, and the desk will keep monitoring feedback from travelers and crew.
